text:
maya (Finance): Heads-up: Contractor Buenavista SRL sent invoice BV-109 for $9,250. Invoice says billing entity: Buenavista SRL (AR) CUIT 30-12345678-9 but also includes a "gross-up for any withholding" clause and a line: 'If Redwood withholds local taxes, Redwood will gross-up net payment.' Can we pay as-is?
carlos (AP-LATAM): Hold payment. We don't generally accept gross-up on vendor invoices. Do we have PO? PO 48211 matches. Uploaded PDF: https://drive.redwood/buenavista/BV-109.pdf
payments-bot: PO 48211 matched and approved, but payment blocked by tax flag: "withholding clause present".
julie (Tax): Quick clarifying Qs: 1) Is Buenavista an Argentine legal entity (SRL) providing services from Argentina? 2) Are the services performed onshore (in AR) or remotely from AR to the US? 3) Did they include any tax residency certificate?
maya (Finance): Vendor included a one-page PDF labelled "tax_note.pdf" that says they're Argentinian and "will require our gross-up for any impuesto a las ganancias / perceived withholdings." No TRC attached.
julie (Tax): OK. Two tracks: if they are an Argentinian entity providing services in Argentina, local law may require us to withhold certain taxes (percepciones/retentions) at payment. In that case vendor cannot unilaterally force a gross-up; commercial negotiation required. If they claim US tax residency (unlikely for SRL), they should provide a W-9. If foreign, they should provide an Argentinian tax residency cert or equivalent TRC and clarify withholding treatment.
dan (Legal): We decline the gross-up clause as a standard policy. It's a transfer of tax risk to Redwood. Ask them to remove it. If they insist, Procurement can negotiate commercial compensation but Legal approval required.
carlos (AP-LATAM): Action items for maya: 1) Ask vendor to reissue invoice without gross-up clause. 2) Request a tax residency certificate (TRC) or Argentinian tax ID evidence (official regs). 3) Ask vendor to confirm where services were performed (AR/remote) and whether they're requesting any retroactive VAT/VAT-like adjustments.
buenavista (vendor) (via email, pasted): "We operate from Buenos Aires; some work was done remotely for your US engineering team. Local brokers told us Argentina may require perceived tax withholdings on cross-border services. We added gross-up to avoid net loss. We will provide a nota fiscal?"
julie (Tax): Note: Argentina's withholding/perception regime can be nuanced; perceived taxes are often applied to certain payments. We need their official CUIT verification (AFIP lookup) and, if available, a certificate showing tax residency. If they cannot provide TRC, we'll proceed to withhold per local rules and remit. We will not gross-up.
dan (Legal): I'll draft a short template reply: decline gross-up, request reissue and residency docs, and state Redwood will apply withholding if legally required.
maya (Finance): Sent vendor: "Please reissue invoice without the gross-up clause, attach CUIT verification and any tax residency/TRC. Confirm whether the services were rendered in Argentina or remotely. If you cannot provide residency evidence, Redwood will withhold and remit applicable local taxes as required by law"
buenavista (vendor) (reply): "We will reissue without gross-up and attach AFIP CUIT confirmation within 48 hours. Thank you." :thumbsup:
carlos (AP-LATAM): Marking invoice on hold until we receive reissued PDF + CUIT/TRC. I'll unlock payment once docs verified and PO matches.
julie (Tax): If they later ask for gross-up reimbursement of withheld tax, escalate to Legal + Procurement. Default: vendor bears their own local tax obligations unless there's a written commercial agreement.
maya (Finance): Thanks team. I'll follow up in 48 hours and update thread. :white_check_mark:
